links.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of ChatGPT responses versus recommended patient reading level
links.effect: AAO-HNS CPG FRES 62.4 ± 16.6; ChatGPT-3.5 39.1 ± 7.3 and ChatGPT-4.0 42.8 ± 8.5 failed the FRES ≥60 standard. All platforms exceeded the recommended FKGL of 6 or lower.
links.quote: AAO-HNS CPG FRES (62.4 ± 16.6) demonstrated an appropriate readability score of at least 60, while both ChatGPT-3.5 (39.1 ± 7.3) and 4.0 (42.8 ± 8.5) failed to meet this standard.

links.outcome: Plain-language readability of AI-generated patient education responses
links.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 FRES 39.1 ± 7.3 and ChatGPT-4.0 42.8 ± 8.5, below the score of 60; all FKGL means exceeded the recommended level of 6 or lower.
links.quote: All platforms had FKGL means that exceeded the recommended level of 6 or lower.

links.outcome: Presence of misleading information in ChatGPT responses to Ménière's disease FAQs
links.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 misleading in 5 of 16 responses and ChatGPT-4.0 in 3 of 16 (31.3% vs 18.75%, P = .6851).
links.quote: ChatGPT-3.5 was misleading in 5 responses whereas ChatGPT-4.0 was misleading in 3 (31.3% vs 18.75%, P = .6851).

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT-3.5 and 4.0 outputs for Ménière's disease patient FAQs against clinical practice guidelines and assesses readability and misleading content, but does not test a deployment practice or guardrail.
